transcript: She let the handles down until the legs took the weight, gently, and she felt the load go off her into the ground. Her mother put her hand out, her left one, slowly, the same as in the night. Well, said her mother eventually, there you are. It takes days. Your jar's where it was. It was not strength. Somebody had pulled them off and stood them against the wall, side by side with the laces tucked in, and she knew without needing to think about it that it had been her mother, left-handed, and that it had taken a long time. This was a whole fight's worth of husks, forty or fifty of them, lying in the seams of a road where Katori had put them down one after another at dusk. She's sore, said Otto. That, said Katori, is what Pell was going to ask you at supper.
